problems.source_says: The methods report a 100-person study and randomized allocation of 45 controls and 55 AI-access participants, but the output analysis does not reproduce those counts. Figure 4b contains 43 Human-User circles, 29 LLM-Influenced triangles and 27 LLM crosses: 99 essay observations, excluding legend symbols. These are derived counts from the PDF vector graphics, not a printed N. Figure 6 independently corroborates this grouping: its for/against/neutral percentages equal the rounded fractions 14/43, 12/43, 17/43; 9/29, 7/29, 13/29; and 6/27, 3/27, 18/27. Thus the figure has 56 AI-access writers rather than the reported 55, and 29 low-use writers rather than the reported 28. No participant flow, exclusion totals or explanation reconciles these discrepancies. The caveat in the form does not establish 100 as an analyzed count; a reconciled overall analyzed N remains unknown (null). The 99 plotted observations establish the size of this particular essay analysis, not a verified total across all outcomes.

problems.form_value: The pilot is reported as n = 8 and its data were analyzed to identify two usage patterns. No pilot allocation counts, exclusions or outcome-specific Ns are stated. It precedes and is separate from the main n = 100 sample; its people are not added to S1 (p. 5, Section 3.1).
problems.source_says: The paper reports a preliminary eight-person pilot before the full experiment and describes analyzing its data. This establishes a separate study phase, but it does not explicitly say whether any pilot participants returned for the main study or whether such participation was prohibited. The form's assertion of a separate participant sample is therefore not fully supported as a claim of nonoverlapping people. Participant overlap remains unknown (null); not adding eight to the main-study count is appropriate.

confirmed.statement: S1 reports individual random assignment of 100 Prolific participants: 45 to no LLM and 55 to AI access. These are people, not ratings or generated texts; the assignment counts themselves are explicitly supported.

confirmed.statement: S1 alone exceeds 50 analyzed writers: the design asks each participant for one essay, and Figure 4b analyzes 99 essay observations across its three mutually exclusive writing-source groups. This eligibility conclusion does not require adding the pilot, archived students or reviewers.
confirmed.locator: p. 4, Section 3.1; p. 8, Figure 4b, caption and PDF vector markers; p. 10, Section 4.3 calls the stance shares proportions of users.

confirmed.statement: The 28/55 LLM-Influenced and 12/55 non-generating users are explicitly reported usage classifications within the AI-access condition, not additional randomized arms. They do not establish analyzed arm denominators; keeping those overall arm counts null is warranted by the unresolved reporting conflict.
confirmed.locator: p. 5, Section 3.1, primary-study classification paragraph; pp. 8 and 10, Figures 4b and 6.

confirmed.statement: No actual exclusion or attrition totals are reported. The control instructions warn of nonpayment for prohibited AI use, but do not report how many cases were affected. Figure 12 explicitly attributes incomplete demographic totals to item nonresponse, which does not establish essay-analysis attrition.
confirmed.locator: p. 22, Appendix A.4; p. 26, Figure 12; full methods/results and appendices through p. 95.

confirmed.statement: S2 reuses 86 university students from ArgRewrite-v2, and the analysis includes all 86 source essays. D1 and human-revised D2 are repeated drafts from the same students; model revisions add no human participants. No corpus exclusions are stated.
confirmed.locator: pp. 5-6, Section 3.1, ArgRewrite-v2; p. 7, Section 3.2, PCA of Embedding Representations.

confirmed.statement: S2 shares its source sample with Kashefi et al. (2022), Argrewrite v.2: an annotated argumentative revisions corpus, DOI 10.1007/s10579-021-09567-z. The saved paper identifies no other publication sharing the newly recruited S1 sample; this is not proof of nonoverlap.
confirmed.locator: pp. 4-6, Section 3.1; p. 18, Kashefi et al. reference.

confirmed.statement: S3 analyzes 18k reviews of 9k matched papers, with 9k human-written and 9k LLM-written reviews. These are output counts; unique reviewers and randomized people are not reported, so the form's null people counts are appropriate. Table 1 further scales review denominators by three potential labels, not by people.
confirmed.locator: p. 6, Section 3.1, Peer Reviews; p. 13, Figure 11; p. 46, Table 1 caption.

confirmed.statement: S4 reports an eight-person protocol pilot and analysis of its usage behavior. Pilot randomization, arm sizes and exclusion totals are not stated, and the pilot alone cannot meet the 50-person threshold.

summary: The PDF does not support S1's exact analyzed N of 100: Figure 4b contains 99 essay observations, and pilot/main participant nonoverlap is also unconfirmed. Criterion 2 still holds because S1 alone analyzes more than 50 writers.
